feedback: Semantic errors: (u0, holding_box & box_fell) -> u0 is unreachable/contradictory since box_fell and holding_box never hold together, so the intended 'box was held' state never gets set. (u1, box_fell & !holding_box) -> u0 then mislabels: a fall in u1 means the box was held and dropped/fell, but the agent returns to u0 instead of a state tracking 'pick it up again', and re-pickup in u0 resets the fall-recovery progress. Consequence: a fall occurring after first pickup erases holding_box credit and the reward for re-picking up is misplaced (reward 0.1 fires on the contradictory conjunction, effectively never; the (u1, box_fell & !holding_box) transition to u0 gives no reward for picking the box back up in u1 either, since the transition label is the fall, not the pickup). Reachability: state u1 is reachable via holding_box, but the machine cannot distinguish 'held box, not yet fallen' from 'box recovered after fall', so the task 'every time the box falls, pick it up again' has no states/rewards encoding the re-pickup requirement; if a second fall happens after re-pickup, the machine again loses track. Missing handling: after a fall in u1, the agent returning to u0 and then picking up gets (u0, holding_box & !box_fell) -> u1 with no reward, so no dense progress signal for the mandated re-pickup; the reward for recovery should be on that transition. Also missing: the else self-loop in u0 covers at_exit without holding_box, fine, but there is no penalty/0 reward for exiting without the box, which is acceptable, yet there is no explicit reward distinguishing correct re-pickup after fall from initial pickup. Suggested fix direction (not a rewrite): use states like u_init (no box yet), u_held (holding box), u_fallen (box just fell, must re-pick), u_done (accepting); reward re-pickup transition u_fallen -> u_held, and exit reward only from u_held; handle multiple falls by re-entering u_fallen from u_held on box_fell.
